messages:
Sara Chen: seeing sustained 504s from the edge for hosted API since ~14:12 UTC. Impact looks broad but not total — a lot of customer requests are hitting 504s at p50-p95 and a few p99s. Request IDs: r=K2jf, r=K2jg, r=K2jk. No config deploys on edge around that time from my side. Anyone else seeing this?

reliability-bot: ALERT: edge.gateway.504_rate increased by 380% in us-west-2 (14:11:40 UTC). Summary: Envoy upstream request timeouts and connection queueing.

Alex P: can you paste a quick repro curl and some envoy log lines? also which cluster is timing out (auth, backend, model-host)?

Sara Chen: quick curl I'm using to repro (non-sensitive):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hi"}' "https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
```
Responses are immediate 504s with no body sometimes, sometimes a small "upstream request timeout".

Mike R: grabbing envoy logs now. attaching a few snippets from the edge proxy logs (sensitive ids redacted):
```
[2024-06-12T14:11:58Z] "POST /v1/generate" 504 - "route: /v1/generate" upstream_reset_before_response: true, details: upstream.request_timeout, upstream_host: models-backend-01:443, request_id=K2jf
[2024-06-12T14:12:05Z] "POST /v1/generate" 504 - "details: upstream.connection_failure" upstream_host: auth-cache-01:443 request_id=K2jg
[2024-06-12T14:12:11Z] "POST /v1/generate" 504 - "details: upstream.response_timeout" upstream_host: models-backend-02:443 request_id=K2jk
```
Looks like two categories: backend model hosts timing out and auth service connection failures.

Lucy Ops Bot: k8s/cluster metrics snapshot (us-west-2) around spike: edge-proxy cpu steady, envoy h2 connection pool exhausted metrics: active_streams > configured max (x3), pending_requests queue depth spiked. Auth-cache pods showed high socket wait and increased latency to 400-800ms.

Ben G: pointer: we've seen this pattern before when the auth service had a cache miss storm and we fell back to identity-service, which couldn't handle the surge — this causes h2 pool starvation at the edge because connections stay open waiting. Two mitigations we can do quickly:
- enable auth caching TTL bump (short-term) so repeated keys hit cache instead of upstream identity check
- increase envoy upstream connection pool for auth cluster (h2 MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS) to drain queue faster

Alex P: agree. Also think we should add a temporary route-level 10s timeout to models-backend to avoid long tail holding edge threads. And can we route auth calls to the read-replica cluster (auth-cache-read) instead of primary for this window?

Mike R: I've started a limited canary to auth-cache-read for 5% of traffic and bumped auth cache TTL to 45s for now. Also increased max_concurrent_streams on the auth cluster from 100->200. Rolling this in across us-west-2 now.

Sara Chen: steps to reproduce for SRE/Support docs: hit /v1/generate in a tight loop with an auth header that forces cache miss (unique token each request). Observed: pending queue climbs, envoy returns upstream.request_timeout and connection failures. Reproducer script attached below: 
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer unique-$i" -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hi"}' https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
This reproduces in ~30s on a medium test cluster.

Lucy Ops Bot: metric update after config changes: pending_requests queue depth down 80% in 2m, 504 rate back to baseline in canary region.

Ben G: nice. Next steps:
- keep TTL bump + pool increase for 2h, monitor
- prepare an auth-cache config that surfaces graceful degraded responses (simple allow with limited rate) as last rescue if identity is fully down
- schedule a functional test to ensure long-tail model requests don't hold up auth connection pools (work with devex)
Assigning oncall: @Mike R to own short-term mitigation, @Alex P to coordinate config PR for increased timeouts and routing.

Alex P: I'll open the PR for route timeout and auth cluster read-replica routing. Putting a note in the deploy window that this is a mitigation change (non-breaking).

Mike R: oncall acknowledged. I'll watch for regressions; if 504s resurface we'll rollback the read-replica route and throttle incoming traffic at the edge.

Sara Chen: customer-facing summary for support: "We observed an auth cache miss storm that caused edge connection queueing and upstream timeouts resulting in intermittent 504s for hosted API. We've deployed a short-term TTL bump and increased connection pool sizes; a canary routing to read-replica is reducing errors. We're monitoring and will follow up with a permanent fix (caching behavior + graceful fallback)."

Ben G: :thumbsup: add a line to the incident timeline and mark as "investigating -> mitigated".

reliability-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations deployed (auth-cache TTL bump, increased h2 pool, 5% canary to auth-cache-read). 504 rate decreased to baseline (14:16 UTC).

Sara Chen: closing thread for now, will reopen if anything flares. Thanks all. :eyes:
